props.title: Center and Mirror

B19.capture_spec: C09: Lab sprite (--sprite-tex sprite), lab-shaders/07-scale.gdshader. Keyframes (L about 11.2 s): zoom = 1 until 0.24 L, then 1 to 0.5 over 0.24-0.66 L, hold. Render L + 1 s, 30 fps, Forward+. End state probes (fill-window): (0.5, 0.5) stage, (0.9, 0.9) teal, (0.8, 0.88) cream (the left eye).
B19.visual_intent: Act title 'Center and Mirror' (serif 40) top-left. Code card at left with the scale shader; at right a real Godot window where, as zoom falls from 1 to 0.5, the sprite swells and slides toward the bottom right of its fixed square until only an arc with one eye remains.
B19.motion_claim: The picture grows but drifts away from the top left corner and out of frame.

show.event: uv = UV * zoom highlighted
zoom falls to 0.5; the picture swells toward the bottom right
an arc and one eye remain: toward the corner

B19.why: The unwelcome result (the picture swelling out of frame) is best seen on the real picture before the explanation.

B20.visual_intent: Two side-by-side panels. Left, labelled 'corner is zero': a small pattern (a cream square with the teal sprite icon) at the panel's top-left corner with a terracotta pivot dot on the corner. Right, labelled 'middle is zero': the same pattern centered with the pivot dot at its middle. Tag on each pivot: 'zero'.
B20.motion_claim: On the left the pattern grows away from the corner; on the right the same pattern grows in place.

show.event: left panel with the pivot at the corner
the pattern scales up, away from the corner
right panel with the pivot in the middle
the same pattern scales in place

B20.runner_up: ShaderLab with an overlay dot at zero
B20.why: Scaling about two different pivots side by side is a geometric mechanism; only a drawing can show the same pattern growing away from the corner and in place.

B21.capture_spec: C10: Lab sprite (--sprite-tex sprite), lab-shaders/11-zoom-centered.gdshader. Keyframes (L about 8.8 s): zoom = 1 until 0.62 L, then 1 to 0.5 over 0.62-0.92 L, hold. Render L + 1 s, 30 fps, Forward+. End state probes (fill-window): (0.5, 0.5) teal, eyes at (0.3, 0.38) and (0.7, 0.38).
B21.visual_intent: Code card at left with the centered zoom shader; at right a real Godot window where, as zoom falls from 1 to 0.5, the sprite grows in place around the middle of its square until the two eyes are large.
B21.motion_claim: The picture grows around its own middle and stays put.

show.event: subtract a half
scale
add it back; then the picture grows in place

B21.why: The fix on the same picture, side by side with the corner version: it now grows in place, with the line in view.

B22.visual_intent: A square with 0 to 1 labels at its corners, (0, 0) top left and (1, 1) bottom right. A tag 'x 2' then 'minus 1' appears; the labels animate to (-2..2) then to (-1, -1) top left, (1, -1) top right, (-1, 1) bottom left, (1, 1) bottom right, with a terracotta dot at the middle labelled (0, 0). The left half and the top half get a small 'negative' tag.
B22.motion_claim: The corner labels slide from 0-1 to minus one to one and the dot settles at the middle, labelled zero, zero.

show.event: the square with 0 to 1 labels
labels double (x 2)
labels shift (minus 1): minus one to one
middle dot (0, 0); left and top tagged negative

B22.why: Labels morphing from 0..1 to minus one..one with the middle becoming zero is the transform; the sign shader adds nothing the labels do not already say.

cues.label: length: the length of a vector; of an offset, the distance

B23.capture_spec: C11: Lab sprite (--sprite-tex white), lab-shaders/12-disc.gdshader. Keyframes (L about 11.9 s): radius = 0.15 until 0.10 L, then 0.15 to 0.8 over 0.10-0.85 L, hold. Render L + 1 s, 30 fps, Forward+. End state probes (fill-window): (0.5, 0.5) and (0.85, 0.5) teal, (0.95, 0.5) and (0.9, 0.9) stage.
B23.visual_intent: Code card at left with the disc shader; at right a real Godot window where a teal disc grows in the centered square as the radius readout sweeps from 0.15 to 0.8.
B23.motion_claim: The disc grows from the middle as the radius dial turns.

show.event: if (length(p) < radius) highlighted
closer than the radius is inside
the radius dial; radius = 0.8

B23.runner_up: manim: a circle from a distance
B23.why: A disc growing as the radius sweeps, beside the one-line test, shows 'length is distance from the middle' on real pixels.

B24.capture_spec: C12: Lab sprite (--sprite-tex white), lab-shaders/13-face-one-eye.gdshader. Keyframes (L about 11.9 s): eye_x = 0.3 until 0.30 L, then 0.3 to 0.5 over 0.30-0.75 L, hold. Render L + 1 s, 30 fps, Forward+. Probes (fill-window, eye_x 0.3): (0.65, 0.425) white, (0.35, 0.425) teal (head, no eye).
B24.visual_intent: Code card at left with the one-eye shader; at right a real Godot window with a teal head and one white eye on the right; as eye x sweeps from 0.3 to 0.5 the right eye drifts outward and the left side stays empty. A terracotta ring on the empty left side with the readout 'nothing here'.
B24.motion_claim: The right eye moves; the left stays empty.

show.event: the eye test highlighted; one eye visible
ring on the empty left side
second test? highlighted

B24.runner_up: manim: two circles, one crossed out
B24.why: One eye present and the other missing is the problem as it really looks.

B25.capture_spec: C13: Lab sprite (--sprite-tex white). Material A (lab-shaders/13-face-one-eye.gdshader) until 0.44 L, then --material-at assigns material B (lab-shaders/14-face-two-eyes.gdshader). Keyframes (L about 11.2 s): eye_x = 0.3 until 0.60 L, then 0.3 to 0.5 over 0.60-0.90 L, hold. Render L + 1 s, 30 fps, Forward+. Probes (fill-window): eye_x 0.3: (0.65, 0.425) and (0.35, 0.425) white; eye_x 0.5: (0.75, 0.425) and (0.25, 0.425) white.
B25.visual_intent: Code card at left with the two-eye shader (one added line, p.x = abs(p.x)); at right the real Godot window: the head with one white eye, then, on 'the left half reads exactly like the right', the left eye appears and, as eye x sweeps from 0.3 to 0.5, the two eyes slide apart together. Readouts: '-0.3 to 0.3', then 'both eyes'.
B25.motion_claim: The left eye appears when abs is applied, and both eyes move apart together under one test.

show.event: p.x = abs(p.x) highlighted; one eye still
minus 0.3 becomes 0.3
the left eye appears (material switches)
the eye test: one test, both eyes; the eyes slide apart

B25.why: The left eye appearing the moment abs is applied, then both eyes moving apart together, is the payoff of the previous beat.

B26.visual_intent: A square (the shape) with a dashed vertical line down its middle and two small white eye circles at minus 0.3 and 0.3 on a horizontal centered axis. The left half hinges over the dashed line and lands on the right half; the left eye lands exactly on the right eye. Tag: 'abs: fold'. A small caption 'mirror twins' lands at the end.
B26.motion_claim: The left half swings over the middle line and the left eye lands on the right eye.

show.event: the square, the centre line, two eyes at plus and minus 0.3
the left half folds over the middle line
the left eye lands on the right eye (settled by 0.45)
caption: mirror twins

B26.why: Folding the shape down its middle is a geometric move; a drawing can show the left half landing on the right.

B27.capture_spec: C14: Lab sprite (--sprite-tex sprite), lab-shaders/15-flip.gdshader. Keyframes (L about 11.6 s): flip = 1 until 0.34 L, then a one-frame step to -1, hold. Render L + 1 s, 30 fps, Forward+. Probes (fill-window): flip 1: eye at (0.4, 0.44); flip -1: eyes at (0.4, 0.56) and (0.6, 0.56), (0.4, 0.44) teal. (A sweep through zero is NOT used: at flip 0 the picture is one stretched row, see flip-v-0-look.)
B27.visual_intent: Code card at left with the flip shader; at right a real Godot window where the sprite sits upright, then at the words 'turns upside down' it flips in one step: the two eyes drop below the middle. Readouts 'flip = 1', then 'flip = -1', and a ring on the lowered eyes.
B27.motion_claim: The picture turns upside down in one step and the eyes land below the middle.

show.event: the scale line highlighted; flip = 1; upright
flip = -1; the picture turns upside down
ring on the lowered eyes

B27.runner_up: manim: the sprite icon mirrored across a line
B27.why: The real picture turns upside down at the moment the scale becomes minus one; the eyes dropping below the middle is checkable.
